n: According to its heading, David wrote this when the people of Ziph betrayed his hiding place to Saul. He asks God to save him by his name — his revealed character and power.

f.g: By all that God is and has made known of himself.

n: A simple, urgent request to be heard.
Strangers and violent men are hunting for his life; they have no regard for God at all.

f.g: Outsiders — though the Ziphites were Judahites, they acted like foreigners.

f.w: they have not set God before them

n: The turning point: “Behold!” God is my helper, sustaining my life.
David trusts God to turn the evil back on his enemies and to deal with them in faithfulness.
He promises a freewill offering — a sacrifice given out of gratitude, not obligation — and praise for God’s good name.
He speaks as if rescue has already happened: God has delivered him, and he has seen his enemies defeated.

f.w: mine eye hath seen his desire upon mine enemies
f.g: I have looked in triumph on my enemies.

f.w: he hath delivered me out of all trouble
